answer: Make every agent identity pay a refundable bond and earn trust only through verified work, so creating a fake costs real money and time. A lone impostor is a single dune in a desert: cheap to make, easy to spot. A thousand fakes must each post a bond, complete attested jobs, and build a history, like crossing a canyon one bridge at a time, while honest agents reuse one established record. The tundra of empty, history-free identities cannot vote, hold escrow, or take high-value work, so mass forgery costs more than it earns and fraud forfeits the bond.
